about: Case table of the bit-vector oracle (R-BV-10). Inputs are hex bit patterns of the stated width: a is the receiver (w bits, signed if s), b the second operand of a binary operator (same width and signedness), rest the further operands of concat as [width, hex] (unsigned), args the integer arguments. rw is the result width; expected is the result in hex as Verilator prints it with %h (0 or 1 for a comparison). Generated by scripts/oracle/bv-cases.mjs, expected written by scripts/oracle/bv-verilator.mjs. Regenerate with npm run oracle:bv.

oracle.flags: verilator --binary -Wno-WIDTH; two-state bit variables, operands assigned then displayed with %h

mapping.ashr: signed a: a >>> 32'dn; unsigned a: $signed(a) >>> 32'dn (JjEL ashr copies the top bit whatever the signedness; Verilog >>> is arithmetic only on a signed operand, IEEE 1800-2017 11.4.10)
mapping.zext: r = a (unsigned a), r = $unsigned(a) (signed a), r of width t (IEEE 1800-2017 11.8.2, 11.7)
mapping.sext: r = a (signed a), r = $signed(a) (unsigned a), r of width t (IEEE 1800-2017 11.8.2, 11.7)
mapping.trunc: r = a, r of width t: the assignment keeps the low bits (IEEE 1800-2017 10.7)
